tier: Direct, pay per use at 3x the regional zCloud rate

free_tier.stated: no free sandbox allowance is published: Direct sandboxes are billed by the second at 3x the regional zCloud rate with no fixed fee; a user can start on a Hobby account with no credit card and test the platform in the US-1 Hobby region, but the verification page does not state that sandboxes are available there
free_tier.notes: a zCloud is 0.5 vCPU and 0.5 GB RAM at USD 9.50 per zCloud-month in standard regions, so the sandbox compute rate is USD 28.50 per zCloud-month equivalent before the by-the-second meter; paused sandboxes accrue no compute

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a sandbox, not a stored object

retention.stated: an idle timeout or a maximum lifetime terminates a sandbox; the workspace can be snapshotted at pause or kept on a shared volume, which outlives the sandbox and can be attached to the next one

egress.terms: no extra fee for network traffic in supported regions; some regions cap the included outgoing traffic at 10 GB per month per zCloud, others list it as unlimited. Sandboxes can restrict outbound traffic to IP/CIDR ranges and domains, and internal infrastructure ranges are always blocked.
egress.free_allowance: 10 GB per month per zCloud in some regions, unlimited in US-3, EU-1 and EU-2

interface_detail: a Public API with /sandbox/create and /sandbox/execute, an MCP server, and a Sandboxes dashboard page
tooling: REST API, MCP server and dashboard; sandboxes run any OCI image pinned by digest, and a stock E2B-style workflow can be driven through the API
chaining: a hosted gVisor sandbox whose workspace can be snapshotted or written to a shared object-storage volume and reused in a later sandbox, so a long agent run resumes from retained state; 200 active sandboxes per account is the default safety ceiling

limits.value: 200 active sandboxes per account by default, raisable on request
sandboxes are enabled per account; after signing up the user must ask Quave to turn them on

binding_note: the sandbox capability is not on by default: an account must ask Quave to enable it before the first sandbox can be created, which stops a new user before the 200-sandbox ceiling or the usage meter matters

identity_cost.detail: creating an account is the first gate: the signup screen uses passwordless email ('/continue-with-email') and Google OAuth; Hobby needs no credit card ('no credit card required'). Upgrading to Professional is free but asks for a personal LinkedIn profile link, a company or personal website, a short business description and how the user found Quave.

reliability_note: an idle timeout or maximum lifetime terminates a sandbox rather than pausing it, a terminated sandbox's snapshot remains on the shared volume or object storage, and internal infrastructure ranges are always blocked from sandbox egress
confidence_note: the price, gVisor isolation, lifecycle and identity facts are quoted from first-party product, docs and verification pages read on 2026-11-25; the exact dollar rate is a derived product of the published zCloud price and the published 3x multiplier, and no sandbox was created

notes: A hosted gVisor sandbox on Quave Direct regions at 3x the regional zCloud rate, billed by the second with no fixed fee and no compute charge while paused. A zCloud is 0.5 vCPU and 0.5 GB RAM at USD 9.50 per zCloud-month in standard regions; the agent-sandbox price is therefore USD 28.50 per zCloud-month equivalent. Sandboxes are opt-in per account, and the Hobby free region is for evaluation with no card. Connect runs the same platform on the user's own cloud account for a license starting at USD 399 a month and is a separate offer.
